Same mechanism and same burden of proof as section-reference-external.json:
every entry pins an exact document line, an exact resolved upstream path,
and the exact spec, so it stops applying the moment any of the three moves,
and each carries the reason in `why`. This is not a place to park a
citation that is merely inconvenient to fix -- a citation the document
asserts is CORRECT does not belong here.

exemptions.why: The line quotes a round brief's claim in order to correct it, and the two lines below it state the refutation in this script's own terms: kinematics_base.cpp is 210 lines and never mentions dimension_. Making the quoted citation resolvable would erase what the paragraph reports.

_unresolvable_comment: Every cited path `tools/ci/measure-upstream-citations.py` cannot resolve
against `$MOVEIT2_SRC` or a vendored `--source` root, declared with the
project it names and why this gate does not check it.
The gate used to print these and pass. That is the same silence a skipped
check produces: an unresolvable citation is an UNVERIFIED citation, and a
list of them under a green OK line reads as coverage. So the rule is now
two-sided and both sides are hard failures:
- a cited path that resolves nowhere and is not declared here fails,
which is what stops a typo or a renamed upstream file from quietly
joining the unchecked pile;
- a path declared here that nothing cites any more fails, which is what
stops this file from accumulating claims about a corpus that moved.
`paths` are matched against the cited string EXACTLY as the corpus writes
it, not against the file on disk -- that is deliberate. Two spellings of
the same file are two rows, so shortening or lengthening a citation shows
up here rather than passing silently under a neighbour's declaration.
A declaration is not an exemption from correctness. It records that this
gate has no tree to check the citation against; the citation may still be
wrong, and `oracle` below is the proof that unchecked citations rot --
every one of its 47 was measured drifted. Anything that CAN be pointed at
a pinned checkout belongs in `verify-upstream-citations.sh`'s `--source`
list instead of here.

Indexing fcl needs the tag pinned first.
